$comment: The patch-set record. This is the budget for local divergence from upstream: docs/ELECTRON_APP_PLAN.md §1. A7 in scripts/verify-bundles.mjs diffs core/ and lib/ against upstreamRef and fails the build if the changed file set differs from patchedFiles. Deliberate new patches must be added here; accidental edits must not be.

patches.summary: Drop the up-front JID normalisation, add receipt/received/played blocking, move JID derivation into the switch.
patches.note: RESOLVED UPSTREAM. Merge 4af6cec (upstream/master @ 34f52fc) made core/node_handler.js byte-identical to upstream, so it left patchedFiles — A7 fails on a recorded file that no longer differs. Upstream landed the same fix independently. Their version is stricter in one place: `played` receipts are blocked only `&& isChatBlocked(jid)` rather than unconditionally. Nothing to re-apply and nothing to carry; the entry stays only as the record of why the file is no longer patched.

patches.summary: Delete the isOutgoingMessage = innerHTML.includes('aria-label="You:"') override that broke device badges.

patches.why: interception.js:28 and ui.js:18 both declared and called a top-level `initialize`. Concatenating the two bundles makes the LAST declaration win for the whole script, so interception.js silently called ui.js's version, the WebSocket hook never armed, and nothing errored. Verified: ui.js's `initialize` is referenced nowhere else and never re-invoked, so the rename is safe.

patches.summary: Gate both checkNodeEncoderSanity calls and the byte-compare behind WAdebugMode.
patches.why: checkNodeEncoderSanity did a full decodeStanza + encodeStanza + isEqualArray on every inbound AND outbound frame, purely as a developer self-check, then isEqualArray ran a second time to decide whether to hit `debugger`. Dev-only work on the hot path.
patches.note: WAdebugMode still exposes the full self-check for anyone debugging.

patches.file: core/interception.js, core/multi_device.js, core/utils.js, core/ui.js, core/parsing/binary_reader.js, core/parsing/node_reader_writer.js
patches.summary: Remove 15 live `debugger;` statements (13 removed + 1 inline guard rewritten + 1 removed as part of P3).
patches.why: A `debugger` statement is free with no debugger attached but SUSPENDS execution when DevTools is open. Electron users will open DevTools. The worst sites were interception.js:74 and :703 (every outbound frame) and hookedPromiseError (every unhandled promise rejection anywhere in WhatsApp, installed by default because WALogs = true).
patches.note: Applied as a one-time source transformation in commit d31818b; the script that performed it has been removed, since git history is the record. It only ever touched lines that are exactly `debugger;`, leaving `//debugger;` comments intact. A8 now guards this continuously, so there is no way for it to regress unnoticed.

patches.summary: Hoist `isIncoming` to a declared local in wsHook.before/after instead of assigning it inline at 6 call sites.
patches.why: `isIncoming` was never declared anywhere in the file, so every `isIncoming=false` / `isIncoming=true` argument was an implicit global write — on the per-frame path. The values were correct, but the pattern is a landmine and pollutes the global namespace.

patches.summary: Re-encode the two protobuf files UTF-16 -> UTF-8 (halving them), and strip the UTF-8 BOM from core/ui.js, core/ui_class_names.js and background.js.
patches.why: The UTF-16 -> UTF-8 re-encode is pre-existing (commit 10809c8) and roughly halved the two protobuf files, which is why the byte figures in the plan are ~1.3 MB rather than ~2.6 MB for the main bundle. The BOM strip is new: a BOM is legal JS mid-script but is not something to rely on at a concatenation seam, and it breaks JSON.parse ahead of a JSON literal. The build also strips BOMs on read (scripts/build.mjs readSource) and assertion A10 guards both source and output.
patches.note: background.js still differs from upstream for this reason but is not inside core/ or lib/, so it is not part of the A7 diff.

patches.summary: Make hookLogs()'s WALogger installation resolve with a bounded retry and a null-safe rebuildTemplate, instead of a single unguarded call 2s after injection.
patches.why: Observed at runtime on every launch: 'Uncaught TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading LOG)'. `require("WALogger")` returns null until WhatsApp's webpack bundle registers that module, and upstream ran the install once at a fixed 2s delay with no guard, inside a setTimeout, so the throw was uncaught AND then surfaced through the window.onunhandledrejection hook installed immediately above it.
patches.extraFix: P7b: `originalWALoggerDev` was assigned `.LOG` instead of `.DEV`, so hookedWALoggerDev invoked the log function's original with DEV arguments.
patches.note: Applied as a one-time source transformation in commit d31818b; the script that performed it has been removed, since git history is the record. The log hook exists to stop WhatsApp's own error reports leaking, so it still installs — it just no longer throws when the module is not ready yet, and it gives up quietly after ~20s rather than throwing on the page.

patches.summary: Scope the body-level MutationObserver, short-circuit non-element nodes, and gate the one-shot `getElementsByClassName('two')` probe behind a uiReady flag.
patches.why: ui.js:40 observes document.body with {childList, subtree} and onMutationsObserved calls getElementsByClassName('two') on EVERY added node, which walks that node's whole subtree. Cost is O(mutations x subtree size) and is the dominant steady-state CPU cost — and the dominant cost while the app sits hidden in the tray, because a backgrounded WhatsApp session still churns (other chats' presence, typing indicators, preview updates).
patches.gate: MUST pass the full feature parity matrix (docs §10) before shipping. This is the only patch that changes WHEN UI work happens, so treat a regression as a release blocker.
patches.note: ui.js is already in the patch set via P0b, so this adds no new merge-conflict domain.

patches.summary: Wrap UMD vendor files so they take the browser-global branch instead of the AMD branch.
patches.why: Observed at runtime: `Uncaught ReferenceError: Tether is not defined`, and the whole ui group failed to inject. lib/drop.js, lib/pako.js, lib/pbf.3.0.5.min.js and lib/sweetalert.min.js each begin with a UMD wrapper that prefers `define.amd`. In the extension those files run in the ISOLATED content-script world, where WhatsApp's globals do not exist, so the browser-global branch is taken. The app has ONE world — the page's — and WhatsApp's webpack bundle installs a global AMD `define`, so the same files publish NOTHING. This is a direct consequence of the two-worlds-to-one-worlds difference in §2.2.
patches.severityNote: core/ calls `pako.inflate(...)` as a bare global in three places (utils.js:442, multi_device.js:118, interception.js:751). With pako undefined, every compressed frame throws inside wsHook.before, the catch passes the frame through UNBLOCKED, and the watchdog still reports PROTECTED because the hook did arm. That is a silent receipt leak — the exact failure this project exists to prevent — and nothing throws at load time, because the global is simply absent until the first message arrives.
patches.fix: Each UMD file is wrapped as `;(function(){var define=void 0, exports=void 0, module=void 0;<file>})();`. The three identifiers are declared function-scoped so they SHADOW the page globals without mutating them — assigning window.define = undefined would be undone by a non-writable or accessor property, and would be visible to concurrent code. The IIFE is deliberately non-strict and called with no receiver, so top-level `this` inside the wrapped file is still the global object, which is what the UMD wrapper passes to the factory as `root`.
patches.scope: electron target only — the extension stages raw files, and there the isolated world has no `define`, so it already takes the global branch.

patches.summary: Rewrite the session user agent from Electron's stock form to a real Chrome UA.
patches.why: Observed at runtime: web.whatsapp.com serves a 'WhatsApp works with Google Chrome 100+' page instead of the app, because Electron's UA carries an `Electron/x.y.z` token.
patches.fix: Removes the Electron token and the app's own product token, and substitutes the REAL embedded Chromium version (process.versions.chrome) into the Chrome slot. Deliberately not a newer Chrome than is embedded: claiming one invites feature detection that then disagrees with the actual engine, which is harder to diagnose than a clean block.
patches.scope: This is a browser-gate bypass and NOTHING more. It is not anonymity and not anti-fingerprinting: it changes exactly one signal. Electron remains distinguishable via renderer strings, feature quirks and network fingerprint. Overridable with WAI_USER_AGENT for debugging.
patches.note: The extension targets are unaffected — they run in a real browser and already send a real UA.

patches.summary: Add a local packer for the extension zips, plus A18/A19/A20 to check the packaged artefact.
patches.why: scripts/build.mjs only ever wrote UNPACKED directories. The only zip in the project was produced by .github/workflows/release.yml, so there was no way to produce the artefact you would actually submit to AMO, and no way to reproduce a release locally. Everything about the shipped zip was therefore untested: nothing checked that the archive held exactly the built files, that it carried the right browser's manifest, or that the reproducibility the README advertises still held.
patches.fix: package-ext.mjs reproduces release.yml's zip exactly — commit-date mtime normalisation, LC_ALL=C byte-order file list, zip -X -9 — so a local checksum is comparable with a CI one. The one deliberate difference is that Node produces the file list instead of `find | sort -z | xargs`, which guarantees a single zip invocation at any file count and lets the script refuse to package a directory containing a symlink. Firefox additionally gets a .xpi, a copy rather than a re-zip so the two are provably identical.
patches.assertion: A18 (archive contents == build dir), A19 (manifest inside the zip is the right browser variant), A20 (reproducible across a rebuild)
patches.a20note: A20 deliberately stamps the build directory with a different mtime before each of its two packs. The obvious formulation — pack the same tree twice — passes even against a packer with the mtime normalisation removed, because nothing rewrites the files in between. The property that matters is reproducibility ACROSS a rebuild, so that is what is tested.
patches.scope: extension targets only. The electron target is packaged by electron-builder and is unaffected.

encoding.$comment: core/parsing/protobuf/{WAProto,WhisperTextProtocol}.js were re-encoded UTF-16 -> UTF-8 by commit 10809c8, which halved them. core/ui.js and background.js still carry a UTF-8 BOM. These are not behavioural patches but they do appear in the diff, so they are declared here rather than left as a surprise.
